title: Duplicating a Word in Pair Encoding
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean word $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps and outputs the pair encoding of $(x,x)$: each bit of $x$ doubled, followed by the separator $01$, followed by $x$.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a finite Turing machine over Booleans
Existence of a natural-number constant c
Computes the pair encoding of (x,x) within c(|x|+1) steps on every input
replaced:
There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c$ such that $M$
computes, within $c\,(n+1)$ steps on inputs of length $n$, the function
sending $x$ to the self-delimiting pair encoding of $(x,x)$: each bit of $x$
doubled, the separator bits $0,1$, then $x$.
